en: So Pi Web Access is one extension I would
install to give the Pi Agent more research
and web search capabilities.
Another extension I personally like having
is the Guardrail extension,
or the
Pi Guardrails extension to be precise.
And as always, there are different options.
That's just the one I'm using. So I'll copy
that
to install it, though I already have it, but
this is how you would install it. And what
Pi Guardrails does is it simply adds a tiny
layer
of extra protection to your Pi setup.
Because by default, Pi has unlimited access
to your file system. It can read files,
write files, and also delete files, of
course. And what PiGuardrails does is it
looks for certain commands, for example, rm,
rf commands, which are about deleting entire
folders,
and blocks them by default, showing you a
confirmation prompt right in your Pi session
to
allow or deny this. Now, be aware that an AI
agent can work around that. It could, for
example, write a script that deletes a
folder and execute that script. It could do
stuff like that. It can read a.env file,
which would also be blocked by default, by
also writing a script that opens that file
and copies it to another file with a less
sensitive file name. So it can work around
these restrictions. Nonetheless, they are
nice to have as a first line of defense.
That's how I like to think about them. Now,
with that extension installed,
you can type guardrails onboarding
to bring up that onboarding dialog where you
can
set up some basic settings for the
Guardrails extension.
So you can hit Enter to walk through that
onboarding, choose the recommended defaults,
for example,
then configure whether it's allowed to
access files outside of the folder you're
currently working in, set this to no
restrictions, for example, or force it to
ask before doing that. I'll go with no
restrictions here and then see a recap.
And you can always run guardrails settings
after installing this extension, of course,
to
have a more detailed settings prompt here
where you can tweak some of the settings.
And you can set up advanced policies here
too. The official Guardrails documentation
is the place to learn more about that.
But just installing this extension already
gives you a bare minimum of protection,
which I
like to have.
